plan: Baseline: tests (12) and acceptance (8) all pass.
Contracts: low_stock consumes Inventory.items() correctly (tested through the real Inventory).
Integration: add, remove and report flow with normalised SKUs and later changes (qa/test_integration.py).
Edge cases: empty inventory, threshold 0 and equal to the quantity, a failed call leaves state unchanged, removing exactly the stock then more, a 10**30 quantity.
Acceptance: ACs 001-008 already covered by acceptance/; not duplicated.
Regression, security, performance: discarded (no prior code, in-memory only, not in the architecture).
gaps: A non-str SKU (for example None) raises AttributeError, not ValueError. Section 6 types sku as str and does not specify this, so I did not report it.
Concurrency is a non-goal and was not tested.

advisory.problem: AC-003: the five bad quantities share one test and one final check of the stock. The first failure hides the rest, and the check can't say which call changed the stock. It still catches an implementation that mutates before it raises.
advisory.evidence: An implementation that accepts one bad value, e.g. add("A", True), fails the test, but the error doesn't name the value. Splitting by value with subTest would make failures easier to read.

advisory.problem: AC-002: the calls are all valid except for the SKU, so the test can't show that an empty SKU raises ValueError and not some other error. Nothing in the brief asks for more.
advisory.evidence: No trivial implementation passes: every call needs a ValueError and items() must stay {}.
